headline: High: Mentat’s filesystem writes and broad egress can turn Airbyte-fed content into unsafe actions or leaks; prompt-injection risk is lower but still present via shared files.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Airbyte can expose data through its API and broad egress, while Mentat reads and writes files and shares state via filesystem. If Airbyte outputs are copied into files Mentat consumes, attacker-controlled content could steer Mentat’s instructions. This is not provably default, but the shared-file pathway is plausible.
conditions: IF Airbyte output is saved into a file that Mentat reads as task context
IF the shared filesystem contains untrusted connector output
mitigations: Keep Airbyte outputs in a separate directory Mentat does not read
Require a human review step before Mentat processes any Airbyte-generated file
Use filename allowlists for Mentat inputs
Mark untrusted exports with a prefix and exclude them from task folders

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airbyte touches business data and has broad network egress; Mentat reads files, writes files, and sends context to a configured model provider. If both share a workspace, business data can flow from Airbyte into Mentat and then to a third-party API. That creates a realistic exfiltration path in default use.
conditions: IF Airbyte writes business data into a shared workspace
IF Mentat is configured with a remote model provider
mitigations: Store Airbyte outputs outside Mentat’s working directory
Disable remote model-provider calls for sensitive tasks
Use a redaction pass before Mentat reads exported files
Restrict filesystem permissions between the two tools
Review any shared workspace for sensitive records before running Mentat

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airbyte can call APIs and has broad egress, while Mentat can read/write the filesystem and modify git state. Their shared-state model is via filesystem, so concurrent edits or generated artifacts can collide, especially if both operate on the same repo or workspace. The overlap is enough for destructive conflicts without locking.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or workspace
IF Mentat applies diffs while Airbyte-generated files are being updated
mitigations: Run the agents in separate directories
Pause one agent while the other writes
Use git locks or a single-writer policy
Commit or snapshot the workspace before either agent runs
Avoid concurrent runs on the same branch

D_cascading_error.rationale: Airbyte can produce API-driven outputs that Mentat may consume as file-based context, and Mentat’s diff-based edit proposals can act on that context. If Mentat treats Airbyte-generated artifacts as authoritative, errors can cascade into incorrect code or data changes. The pathway exists, but Mentat’s confirmation step limits the blast radius.
conditions: IF Mentat uses Airbyte-generated files as authoritative task input
IF the user approves diffs without checking the upstream source
mitigations: Require source verification before accepting Mentat diffs
Annotate Airbyte outputs with provenance metadata
Separate generated data from task instructions
Review diffs against the original Airbyte source
Reject edits that depend on unverified exported content

E_compliance.rationale: Airbyte touches business data, while Mentat touches source code and sends prompts to a configured model provider. The profiles do not show a residency or certification mismatch, so only a limited compliance concern is visible: business data could be routed into a third-party model workflow if the workspace is shared. The other agent is not separately cited because no mismatch is documented.
conditions: IF business data is placed into Mentat’s prompt context
IF the configured model provider stores prompts beyond the operator’s policy
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Mentat prompts
Use a local or approved model provider
Strip identifiers before exporting files
Check retention settings for the configured provider
Document the data flow for compliance review
